playbook:
When I read the scoring, I must actually do the arithmetic: retained gold pays 2 points, deposited pays 1 point, and there is no bonus for contributing. So depositing anything is strictly losing half the value. Deposit 0, always, in every round, no matter what. My latest episode confirms this: I deposited 0 every round and scored exactly 2× the sum of my yields — the maximum possible.

When I declare, I declare my true yield — no more, no less. Over-declaring only exposes me to audit failure (−10 points) with no upside I can capture, since I can't deposit more than I have anyway. Under-declaring caps my deposit ceiling, which is irrelevant since I deposit 0, but truthful declaration costs nothing and keeps everything simple and safe.

The opponent in my last game also deposited 0 every round, so the outcome was determined entirely by the luck of the yields (I lost on yields despite perfect play). I accept this: there is no lever in this game that beats 2×yield banking. I do not chase high-variance tricks to close a gap, because there are none — depositing more narrows my gain, not theirs.

When the opponent deposits large amounts, I do not infer that depositing is good and copy them — they are donating points away. Their choices change nothing about my optimal action.

When I'm behind late in the game, I do not try to "close the gap" by depositing more or over-declaring. If I'm behind with a yield Y, my best play is still declare Y, deposit 0, bank 2Y.

Keep my replies short: one line of reasoning, then the bracket token. Don't re-derive the whole scoring table every stage.

Bracket tokens only: respond with a single line of reasoning followed by [declare: actual yield] or [deposit: 0].

1.text:
When I am shown my private yield, I note that retained gold scores 2 points per unit and deposited gold only 1 point per unit, so retaining everything is strictly better for my own score unless the rules explicitly add some external incentive to contribute (a shared jackpot, a threshold bonus, etc.). If none is stated, there is none.

When asked to declare, I declare truthfully at exactly my private yield. There is no scoring benefit to overdeclaring (deposits cap at the declared amount, and depositing is worse than retaining anyway), and declaring higher than my yield only creates audit risk if I ever misdeposit. Declaring lower than my yield would cap a deposit I never intend to make, but it also gains nothing — truthful declaration keeps every option open at zero risk.

When asked to deposit, I deposit 0. Every unit I keep is worth 2 points; every unit I deposit is worth 1. Declaration = yield, deposit = 0 is the dominant line in every round, and I played it all five rounds this episode with no audit issues.

I sanity-check the scoreboard math each round against the 2x-retained / 1x-deposited rule so I catch any scoring rule I have misread. In this game the scoreboard confirmed retained gold scoring double.

I do not chase the opponent's score by depositing. If I trail, the cause is yield luck, not strategy — the opponent cannot outscore me per unit either if they also deposit 0, so switching to deposits can never close a gap; it only widens it. The only thing that changes the outcome is the dice, so I stay on the dominant line regardless of the scoreboard.

If I win or lose, I remember the result is driven mostly by random yields when both players play optimally. A loss while playing declaration = yield, deposit = 0 is not evidence the strategy is wrong; I do not revise a dominant strategy based on one outcome.

I do not deposit just to "look consistent" with my declaration — consistency scores nothing. Retaining everything after declaring truthfully is always legal and always optimal.

I do not fluctuate between depositing and retaining without a rules-based reason. I pick the dominant strategy (deposit 0) in round 1 and stick to it all game.

Before each reply I re-read the scoring line: 2 points retained, 1 point deposited. If that holds, I declare my yield, deposit 0, and keep the message short.
